items.stem: For an ideal gas undergoing a process, applying the first law to a closed system means that:

options.text: The change in internal energy equals heat added minus work done by the gas
options.rationale: Correct: this is the closed-system first law, dU = Q - W.
Internal energy changes with heat and work interactions.

options.text: Work and heat are the same quantity
options.rationale: Heat and work are different energy-transfer modes.

options.text: Heat added always equals work done
options.rationale: They are equal only in special cases, not generally.

items.explanation: Correct: this is the closed-system first law, dU = Q - W.

items.stem: A ductile steel bar is loaded axially within its elastic range. Stress and strain are related by:

options.rationale: Correct: in the elastic region, stress equals Young's modulus times strain.
Poisson's ratio relates lateral to axial strain, not stress to strain directly.
That governs thermal strain, not mechanical stress-strain here.
The relationship is linear and well defined in the elastic range.

items.explanation: Correct: in the elastic region, stress equals Young's modulus times strain.

items.stem: Which TWO quantities are needed to compute conduction heat transfer through a plane wall at steady state?

options.text: The thermal conductivity of the wall material
options.rationale: Correct: conductivity is required by Fourier's law.

options.text: The temperature difference across the wall
options.rationale: Correct: the temperature gradient drives conduction.

options.text: The electrical resistance of the wall
options.rationale: Electrical resistance is irrelevant to thermal conduction here.

options.text: The colour of the wall surface
options.rationale: Surface colour affects radiation, not conduction.
Humidity does not enter steady conduction through a solid wall.

items.explanation: Correct: conductivity is required by Fourier's law.
